title: remove(int) or remove(Object)?

blocks.text: `List<Integer>` has two `remove` overloads: `remove(int index)` removes the element at a position, and `remove(Object o)` removes the first element equal to `o`. Passed an `int`, the call picks `remove(int)`, the exact match, before boxing is ever tried.
Write `removeValue(List<Integer> values, int value)` in `Removal`. It removes the first element equal to `value` and returns whether one was removed:

items: a value not in the list removes nothing: `removeValue(values, 99)` returns `false`;
only the first equal element goes: `[5, 7, 5]` becomes `[7, 5]`.

cases.says: Removing 20 from [10, 20, 30] leaves [10, 30]: 20 is a value, not a position.
Removing 9 from [0, 1, 2] returns false and removes nothing.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

concepts: Overloads that differ by a primitive and an object, like List.remove(int) and remove(Object), are a trap: an int argument picks the primitive one.
